terms.gloss: unasked, of one’s own accord; making the first move
evidence: Ter. Eun. 813: ubi nōlīs, cupiunt ultrō
Publil. Sent. B 1: ultrō sī offerās
terms.comment: Lewis & Short draws the line: ultrō faciō, nōn rogātus; sponte faciō, nōn coāctus neque adjūtus. So ultrō is acting unasked, and goes with offering, coming forward, starting a fight. Its literal sense is “beyond, to the far side” (ultrō citrōque, to and fro).

terms.gloss: on my (your, his) own initiative; unforced
terms.grammar: phrase: ablative of the defective noun spōns with the possessive
terms.comment: Without compulsion or help, by one’s own will, or of a thing, by itself (see own).

phrases.latin: Bis est grātum quod opus est, ultrō sī offerās.
phrases.english: what is needed is twice welcome if you offer it unasked

phrases.latin: nē exspectēmus quidem, dum rogēmur; studium semper adsit, cūnctātiō absit
phrases.english: let us not even wait to be asked; let there always be eagerness and never hesitation

phrases.latin: Nōlunt ubi velīs; ubi nōlīs, cupiunt ultrō.
phrases.english: when you want it, they don’t; when you don’t, they want it of their own accord

phrases.latin: movērī vetuisse puerum dōnec suā sponte experrēctus esset
phrases.english: she forbade them to move the boy until he woke up of his own accord

phrases.latin: Nēmō tē rogāvit, et tamen ultrō adjūvistī.
phrases.english: Nobody asked you, and yet you helped of your own accord.
